about: Maps the free-text reason of a SKIP result to a class. Runs recorded under the cited-notOffered rule (results.json `notApplicableRule`, docs/04 section 8) are not applicable only where the SKIP carries `evidence` (a cited notOffered entry of the adapter); a rule here that gives not-applicable to any other SKIP of such a run gives not-reached. Older runs keep the class their reason gives. Rules are tried in order; the first match wins. A reason that matches nothing is reported as unclassified so that it gets a rule. Classes: not-applicable (the platform does not implement the task or feature, so the check does not apply); not-reached (the platform may well do it, but our test setup cannot drive it yet); version-mismatch (the platform offers the task at a different version than the check needs); out-of-tier (a stricter-tier check outside the headline tier; not counted at all). The special class by-served-slug resolves a 'type not declared' reason from the run data: version-mismatch when some other version of the same task did run, otherwise not-applicable. Where a class is a most likely reading rather than a fact, the note says so. Latest-version focus (D245, 2026-11-20): the classes here are the at-a-glance classes of a result. On the reach pages (the coverage matrix, docs/28, the platform pages) a SKIP is also read by the version it names: a SKIP of an older version (below the latest of its task) or of a retired latest version is reach class `scope` (outside the target), never `platform`; only a SKIP at the latest non-retired version is `platform`. Sweep rule (2026-11-15, final2): a not-reached SKIP must name the specific, checked reason it could not be driven (a test-host limit, a missing trigger, a clock that cannot be set), never only that the adapter lacks a capability; surface-scoped rules carry that evidence in their note.

rules.note: The live community container offers no proof-verification entry on its wire (the in-process host does), so the checks that read the verifier's own verdict were not reached on the live row (docs/35).
The vector needs the harness to set the presentation nonce the service will accept; the live container does not expose that control, so the check was not reached on the live row (docs/35).
The community's push records are in its store, not on its wire, so a live row cannot observe a push (docs/35, class D).

rules.match: ^(tier [0-9] not selected|only runs at tier|implementation claims tier)
rules.note: Stricter-tier check outside the headline tier.

rules.match: ^window difference: the row pins the profile window
rules.note: Tier 2 (attested profile) rows that pin the profile acceptance window; the implementation declares a different window, which the framework allows. Recorded at Tier 2 only (checked in the final2 run folders: keyring-wallet clockSkewSeconds 300, VTI agent service maxAgeSeconds 600).

Essential governance (decision 39, docs/04 section 19): the platform's declared authority set has one member, so a check that needs two or more approvers does not apply. Evidence: the declared E recorded in the run's run.json (implementations[].essentialGovernance).

Essential governance (decision 39): the platform declares minApprovals 1, so a check that needs an approval before completion (or a repeat before it) does not apply. Evidence: the declared E in run.json.

Essential governance (decision 39): the adapter states no readable authority set and minApprovals (GOV-NOT-PROBED); the platform may well behave per its E, but the harness cannot drive the per-declared-E checks without it. The reason names why E is unreadable.

rules.match: ^(authority set not drivable by the harness|no harness actor outside the declared authority set)
rules.note: Essential governance (decision 39): E is declared, but a member is not a harness identity (or no harness identity lies outside the set), so the harness cannot send the approvals. The reason names the member.

Checked in VTI's proof library at the tested ref (affinidi-data-integrity 0.8.0, src/crypto_suites.rs: ecdsa-jcs-2019 is 'P-256 only', because the pipeline hashes with SHA-256 unconditionally). VTI does not offer P-384 under this suite.

Checked in the witness server: its adapter hosts the two witness session tasks only (witness/session and witness/session/submit); the generic framework, credential-exchange, ceremony and two-phase vectors need a carrier task the server does not host (and the proof and receipt verification vectors a verifier capability its adapter does not offer), so they do not apply to this surface.
Checked in the wallet: it signs and verifies eddsa-jcs-2022 only (documentProof.ts); no ecdsa-jcs-2019 suite at any curve.
The suite's reference adapter implements eddsa-jcs-2022 only (src/adapters/reference/reference.ts, cryptosuites); the ECDSA vectors are measured on the platforms that declare the suite (VTI).

CER-015 and CER-016 test the suite-local conformance/ceremony/status task, which the default reference row does not offer by design; the separate reference-status row (`--adapter reference-status`, src/runner/cli.ts) declares it and is checked by the tests.

Checked in VTI at the tested ref: the in-process community host is built with TestVtcBuilder (vtc-service/src/test_support.rs), which is tempdir-backed and has no data-directory option, so a restart that keeps the store cannot be driven. The VTC itself persists its store in deployment; this is a test-host limit.

DUP-103 needs a type that accepts a payload member its schema does not name. No VTI type served in process was found to do so (VTI's payload structs use serde deny_unknown_fields widely: 366 sites at the tested ref); not checked type by type, so the class is not-reached rather than not-applicable.

Checked in VTI at the tested ref: the services read the wall clock directly (Utc::now(); 13 call sites counted in the observe-adopt sweep, <results dir>/runs/2026-11-15-observe-adopt-vta-inprocess/README.md) and the in-process hosts offer no clock injection; the runner rebases relative times, but vectors that need an exact instant or several clock offsets cannot be driven without a fake clock (faketime is not available here).

The community service's trust-task route requires a proof on every document and signs its answers (VTI's policy, recorded in src/adapters/vti/adapter.ts), so the unsigned Tier 1 vectors do not apply to it; they are not refusals to be counted as differences.
Not reached in this row only: the same run folder has a second row without the attested option (`nonattested/`, VTI_INPROCESS_NO_ATTESTED=1) that runs these vectors.
Not reached in the reference-attested row only; the plain reference row of the same run runs them.

The default reference row declares no deployment governance on purpose (decision 75 by the project owner: governance is the deployer's choice, never built into the suite); the governance probes run through the reference-governance adapter (docs/17).

No handler for relationship tasks in the tested service (read from its source).
Its consent flow is a different, policy-based flow.

rules.label: send-only
rules.note: The emit surface drives the platform's own message builders and serves no task, so a check that needs a server of the task does not apply to it (resolved from the run data like any type not declared: a different version that ran reads as version-mismatch); the receiving side is measured on the in-process surfaces.

rules.label: no counterpart
rules.note: No implementation answers this task, so the receive check has no host (docs/22).

rules.label: not served by this surface
rules.note: Resolved from the run data: other version ran = different version; nothing of that task ran = not applicable (inferred from the run, not confirmed by the platform's maintainers).

rules.label: not reached by the suite
rules.note: A suite limit, not a platform difference. Checked in the wallet source: the wallet builds these 21 types (rooms blobs, keys file-key and present, records, the rooms offer accept, voting ballot cast, join-request decide, vta contexts get, webvh did delete, vrc relationships issue and propose, witness session and submit), but the suite adapter emit flows (src/adapters/keyring-wallet/) do not drive them. Recorded in the coverage measurement of the wallet (21 CE-* vectors per tier, reason `type not emitted`). Not applicable would say the wallet does not send them, which is not what the source shows.

rules.label: not reached by the suite
rules.note: A suite limit, not a platform difference. VTI builds these four types (rooms blobs chunk 0.1, blobs upload abort 0.2 and commit 0.2, and the community rooms offer accept 0.1; vectors CE-RM-001, CE-RM-003, CE-RM-006 and CE-RM-023) only inside the VTA's rooms/keys/act signing call (`room_act` and `room_act_community`, vta-sdk/src/client/rooms.rs: a host-bound room request the VTA completes), which the suite's emit host cannot drive. The emit survey records the same reading in src/adapters/vti-emit/not-built.json: each is named outside the specification crates only in vta-sdk/src/client/rooms.rs (and vta-service/src/trust_tasks/room_act.rs or policy_gate.rs), with no client builder of its own that the host can call. Not applicable would say VTI does not send them, which is not what the source shows.
The platform's own message builders do not produce this task.
